correctness.rationale: The claim reduces unary automorphism orbits to pointed isomorphism classes of finite one-generated Heyting algebras. Yamamoto explicitly supplies local finiteness and ultrahomogeneity of the Fraïssé limit. Citkin's Rieger–Nishimura classification supplies one finite one-generated algebra Z_n for each n>=2 and the generator-orbit exceptions Z_2, Z_4, Z_5. The two ingredients imply c_2=2 and c_n=1 for n>=3. The bundled checker independently reconstructs the standard finite Z_n through n=20 and verifies the initial generator-orbit pattern.

value.rationale: The automorphism group and age combinatorics of the universal homogeneous Heyting algebra are the motivating objects in Yamamoto's paper. The result pinpoints the first possible arity of non-oligomorphic behavior, gives an exact closed-form unary orbit grading, and identifies the classical Rieger–Nishimura ladder with a natural permutation-group invariant.
